name: application-stale-data-badge
title: Stale Data Badge
description: Small inline 'updated N ago' badge that flags itself stale once elapsed time crosses a threshold, with a compact refresh action — distinct from sync-status-row, which is a full syncing/success/error status row rather than a compact staleness indicator with no sync lifecycle of its own.
useWhen: Showing how recently a piece of data was fetched, inline next to the data itself.
You want the stale/fresh state derived from a real elapsed-time comparison against a threshold.
A compact badge fits better than a full status row with sync lifecycle states.
avoidWhen: You need to represent an active syncing/success/error lifecycle — use sync-status-row instead.
There's no meaningful staleness threshold for the data — a plain timestamp is simpler.
You need a full-width row layout — this badge is sized for inline placement.
responsiveBehavior: The badge sizes to its content and can sit inline next to other elements; multiple badges wrap naturally in a flex container.
accessibility: Stale state is conveyed by both an amber color scheme and a color-shifted status dot, never color alone — the visible 'Updated Nm ago' text is the primary signal.
The refresh button has an explicit aria-label ('Refresh data') independent of the spinning icon.
Elapsed time is computed from real Date values (now - updatedAt), never a hand-typed string that could drift from the actual timestamp.

variants.title: Stale data badge
variants.description: A fresh badge (2 minutes old, under the 5-minute threshold) beside a stale badge (12 minutes old, past the threshold), on a light surface.
accessibility: Elapsed minutes are computed as Math.floor((now - updatedAt) / 60000), never hand-typed independently of the two timestamps.

variants.title: Stale data badge (Dark)
variants.description: The same fresh and stale badge pair, adapted for dark surfaces.
accessibility: Badge colors meet WCAG AA contrast on dark backgrounds.
